patterns.note: An asymmetric, dynamic grid layout for project showcases, where images and titles appear to fill the screen as the user scrolls, rather than a fixed, uniform grid.
Prominent, widely spaced sans-serif text is used for the primary navigation, creating a strong visual hierarchy against the minimalist background.
A high-contrast black and white palette dominates the design, with a single vibrant orange accent color reserved exclusively for primary calls to action.
The initial tall header with widely spaced navigation items condenses and becomes sticky at the top of the viewport after a short scroll, maintaining its large text size.
Project images and their accompanying titles reveal with a subtle fade-in and slight upward slide animation as they enter the viewport during scrolling.

technique_notes: The navigation bar uses a scroll-triggered transformation, reducing its height and becoming fixed at the top of the viewport after a certain scroll depth, while maintaining its content.

Content elements, specifically project images and their associated text, are revealed using CSS keyframe animations, likely involving a slight upward translation and opacity change as they scroll into view.

design_tokens.type_scale: large, bold sans-serif navigation items (~2-3x body) with clear, legible body text and prominent project titles.
design_tokens.radius: sharp — all elements, including images and buttons, feature crisp 0px corner radii.
design_tokens.spacing: airy — generous white space is used, especially in the initial view, creating a sense of openness, with balanced padding around content sections.

standout: The site's design is distinctive for its extreme initial minimalism, presenting a vast amount of white space and a sparse navigation before dynamically revealing a rich, grid-based portfolio of architectural projects. The transformation of the header from a tall, almost decorative element to a compact, sticky navigation on scroll is a key visual cue that transitions the user from an exploratory state to content consumption.
